pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src/features/developer/careShareClient.ts:2 The context's only browser-originated request is a same-origin POST/DELETE to its own owner-self route carrying just the app session cookie, and its data is loaded server-side through Prisma, so no dependency credential reaches the bundle and no broker, public-role grant, loopback gate or courier seal is called for; searches of the context's directories (src/features/developer, src/lib/org, src/app/org/developer, src/app/org/[slug]/developer, src/components/org/shell, src/app/api/me/mentor) for createBrowserClient, anon_key, x-api-key, createHmac and 127.0.0.1 found nothing.

techniques.evidence: src/features/developer/careShareClient.ts:2 No privileged upstream is reached from this context's browser code. The share route is the app's own endpoint, and the browser carries only its session.
src/features/developer/careShareClient.ts:37 The only fetch runs in the browser against a fixed same-origin constant. No server fetch takes its address from data.

src/app/api/me/mentor/share/route.ts:70 No upstream is brokered here. The route's own failures still log the error on the server and return a fixed message ('Failed to store your share.'), so no internal detail reaches the browser.

src/app/api/me/mentor/share/route.ts:62 The browser preview is advisory. The client writes its own share and is the authority over it, so nothing needs a seal, and the server re-runs the validator on every POST rather than trusting the preview's result.
src/lib/org/developer-view-load.ts:11 Contributor rows are read in a server-only loader through the server DB client. No public role reaches a table, so regime one does not hold.

src/lib/org/developer-view-load.ts:35 No row-level policies are involved because the browser never writes to the store directly. The same instinct applies anyway: the owner key comes from the server-resolved identity, never from the request.
